court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Sub Court at Aruppukottai, HMOP No.148 of 2021
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2011 and have a 10-year-old daughter. The husband filed for dissolution of marriage on grounds of desertion, while the wife filed for maintenance. The husband is willing to pay interim maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: Parents are duty bound to maintain their minor children.
legal_principles.held: The 10 year old child has to be taken care of by the father, who is the natural guardian and an earning member.

legal_principles.principle: Courts are bound to consider grant of Interim Maintenance in the interest of minor children and to protect their livelihood.
legal_principles.held: Even in the absence of any application, the Courts are bound to consider grant of Interim Maintenance in the interest of the minor children and to protect their livelihood.

legal_principles.principle: The father being the natural guardian under the Guardian and Wards Act, is bound to maintain his minor daughter or son by paying maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The father being the natural guardian under the Guardian and Wards Act, is bound to maintain his minor daughter or son by paying maintenance even in such circumstances, where there is a matrimonial dispute or for visitation right.

legal_principles.principle: Courts must act as a custodian of minor children when such children are neglected by either of the parents.
legal_principles.held: Court must act as a custodian of minor children, when such children are neglected by either of the parents.

outcome.final_order: The husband is directed to pay Rs.3,000/- per month as interim maintenance from December 2022 onwards.

use_for_drafting: petition for custody of minor child
